query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Across temperature and strain-rate regimes, the dynamic mechanical behavior of as-solidified Co-free FeNiCrMn (single-phase FCC) is governed by temperature-dependent Mn–Ni–Cr short-range order (SRO) that simultaneously tunes stacking-fault energy (SFE) and imposes solute drag on dislocations. This single mediator produces three regimes: (i) at low temperature and/or high strain rate, reduced effective SFE promotes deformation twinning (TWIP) and high work-hardening; (ii) at intermediate temperature and moderate strain rate, SRO-enhanced solute drag yields dynamic strain aging (DSA) with negative strain-rate sensitivity and serrated flow; and (iii) at high temperature, SRO dissolves and solute drag weakens, restoring conventional dislocation glide/climb with positive strain-rate sensitivity and lower work-hardening. The composition and its strength–ductility balance remain unchanged.
generation.material_initial_state: As-solidified FeNiCrMn alloy, Co-free, nominally single-phase FCC with typical solidification microsegregation but no intentional second-phase precipitation; grain structure representative of a cast product; oxygen/nitrogen kept low; strength–ductility balance comparable to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi retained.
generation.intervention: Apply controlled mechanical loading while varying temperature and strain rate; optionally compare two thermal histories that preserve composition and strength–ductility: (A) solutionized + water-quenched (minimized SRO) and (B) low-temperature aged without precipitation (enhanced SRO).
generation.conditions: Tension (and confirm with compression) at temperatures from cryogenic to elevated (e.g., liquid nitrogen to ~0.6–0.7 Tm of FCC matrix) and strain rates spanning quasi-static to impact-relevant (e.g., ~1e-4 to ~1e3 s^-1). Inert atmosphere for high-T tests to avoid oxidation; identical microstructural state (no prior heavy cold work) across tests.
generation.structural_mediator: Mn–Ni–Cr short-range order that modulates (i) stacking-fault energy and twinning stress, and (ii) solute drag on mobile dislocations; resulting twin volume fraction and planar slip character act as the immediate microstructural mediators of the macroscopic response.
generation.mechanism: At low T/high rate, lower effective SFE and suppressed solute diffusion reduce the twinning stress relative to slip, promoting TWIP and high work hardening while maintaining ductility. At intermediate T/moderate rate, thermally activated solute-dislocation interactions (SRO-driven solute atmospheres) cause pinning–unpinning, giving DSA, serrations, and negative strain-rate sensitivity with reduced uniform elongation. At high T, SRO dissolves and solute drag weakens; dislocation glide, cross-slip, and climb dominate, producing positive strain-rate sensitivity, lower flow stress, and diminished work hardening.
generation.predicted_outcome: A regime map emerges: (1) Low T and/or high strain rate: increased twin density, higher work-hardening rate, rate-strengthening without loss of ductility; (2) Intermediate T at low-to-moderate strain rates: observable serrated flow, negative strain-rate sensitivity (m < 0), increased yield but reduced uniform elongation; (3) High T: disappearance of serrations, positive m, lower yield stress and reduced work hardening. Quenched material (lower SRO) shifts DSA onset to higher T or reduces its magnitude relative to low-T-aged material.
generation.baseline: Quasi-static room-temperature behavior without strong solute drag: predominantly planar slip, modest work hardening, near-zero to slightly positive strain-rate sensitivity, minimal twinning, and absence of pronounced serrations.
generation.boundary: Applies to single-phase FCC FeNiCrMn with minimal interstitial content and no significant second-phase precipitation or heavy prior cold work; if strong microsegregation creates stable secondary phases, or if grain size/texture or interstitials dominate the flow behavior, the SRO/SFE-mediated mechanism may not govern.
generation.uncertainty: Exact temperatures and strain-rate thresholds for regime transitions depend on the actual SFE and SRO state, which are composition- and processing-sensitive; microsegregation and residual interstitials can shift or blur these boundaries.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of the same Co-free FeNiCrMn: (A) solutionized at high T and water-quenched to minimize SRO; (B) low-temperature aged (below precipitation onset) to enhance SRO. Perform tensile tests across temperature and strain-rate matrices. Characterize before/after deformation: EBSD/TEM for twin fraction and slip character; high-speed in-situ XRD or TEM for stacking-fault probability during loading; measure serration metrics and strain-rate sensitivity m; assess SRO via atom probe tomography or diffuse scattering. Compare regime transitions and response between A and B.
measurements: True stress–strain curves across T and strain-rate matrices
Strain-rate sensitivity m and activation volume via stress-relaxation or jump tests
Serration index (density, amplitude) to detect DSA
Twin area/volume fraction and twin thickness via EBSD/TEM
Planar vs wavy slip characterization (TEM faulted bands, SF probability)
SRO indicators (APT clustering statistics, diffuse scattering intensity changes)
Work-hardening rate evolution (dσ/dε) and uniform elongation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if: (i) twin fraction does not increase with decreasing temperature and/or increasing strain rate, or shows no measurable correlation to effective SFE indicators; (ii) no regime exhibits serrated flow or negative strain-rate sensitivity at intermediate temperatures/strain rates despite clear evidence of SRO and solute-dislocation interactions; or (iii) high-temperature tests still show persistent serrations/negative m consistent with strong solute drag after SRO has measurably diminished.
